summary.text: A monsoon is traditionally a seasonal reversal of the wind that comes with a matching change in rainfall.
Monsoons are now seen as a planetary-scale pattern driven by the yearly migration of the Intertropical Convergence Zone between its northern and southern limits.
The word usually means the rainy phase, though there is also a dry phase, and it reached English in British India from a word meaning "season".

facts.label: Word origin
facts.value: Arabic mawsim, meaning "season", via Portuguese monção

facts.label: Major systems
facts.value: West African, South Asian–Australian, North and South American

facts.label: Old explanation
facts.value: A giant sea breeze, no longer accepted

facts.label: Linked uplift
facts.value: The Tibetan Plateau, after India collided with Asia

items.prompt: The English word monsoon traces back through Portuguese to an Arabic word. What did that Arabic word mean?

options.label: Rain
Wind
Storm
Season

items.explain: English monsoon came from Portuguese monção, ultimately from Arabic mawsim, meaning "season".

items.prompt: Scientists once explained monsoons as a huge sea breeze caused by land heating up more than the ocean. What explanation replaced it?

options.label: The yearly north–south shift of the Intertropical Convergence Zone
The ocean's main currents flipping direction each spring
Heat escaping from volcanoes along the coast
The pull of the Moon on the atmosphere

items.explain: The sea-breeze idea is no longer considered the cause; monsoons are now tied to the annual migration of the Intertropical Convergence Zone.

items.prompt: Which slow geological change has been linked to a stronger Asian monsoon?

options.label: The drying of the Sahara
The rise of the Tibetan Plateau
The opening of the Atlantic
The sinking of the Andes

items.explain: A stronger Asian monsoon has been linked to the uplift of the Tibetan Plateau after India collided with Asia around 50 million years ago.

items.prompt: People usually say "monsoon" to mean the rainy season. Technically, what else is part of the same pattern?

options.label: A season of snow
A run of hurricanes
A dry phase
Nothing at all

items.explain: The term usually refers to the rainy phase of the seasonal pattern, although technically there is a dry phase too.

items.prompt: The rain belt behind the monsoon swings between northern and southern limits each year. What sets where those limits lie?

options.label: The phase of the Moon each month
How many earthquakes strike nearby
How much forest grows along the coast
The contrast in heating between land and sea

items.explain: The limits of the Intertropical Convergence Zone vary according to the land–sea heating contrast.

items.prompt: During ice ages, falling sea levels closed the Indonesian Seaway, so cold Pacific water could no longer flow into the Indian Ocean. What is believed to have happened to the monsoons?

options.label: They became more intense as the ocean warmed
They faded away as the ocean cooled down
They reversed and blew only from the land
They moved entirely over to the Pacific

items.explain: With cold Pacific water blocked, Indian Ocean surface temperatures rose, which is believed to have made the monsoons more intense.
